14ft-vs-19ft.description: Compare 14 ft vs 19 ft trucks on payload, volume and rate. On Rourkela–Ranchi (180 km), FTL is ₹15,300–₹21,600 and PTL ₹3,060–₹4,320/tonne. FTL ₹85–₹120/km
14ft-vs-19ft.keywords: 14 ft, 19 ft, truck comparison, which truck to book, PTL truck size

faq.q: How much can a 14 ft vs a 19 ft truck carry?
faq.a: The 14 ft (Tata 407 Gold SFC class) carries up to 2,500 kg over 680 cu ft. The 19 ft (Tata LPT 1109 class) carries up to 5,500 kg over 1,300 cu ft — more than double the payload and nearly double the volume.

The 2026 benchmark class rate is ₹28–₹38/km for 14 ft/17 ft and ₹36–₹48/km for 19 ft/22 ft. The 19 ft costs more per km but moves far more per trip, so per tonne it is usually cheaper when you have the load.

faq.q: Will my load fit a 14 ft truck?
faq.a: Compare your cargo's volume and weight with 680 cu ft and 2,500 kg. If either is exceeded, you need the 19 ft deck. Palletised FMCG (1.2 m pallets) fit 8–10 on a 14 ft deck, 12–14 on a 19 ft deck.

faq.q: What changes for loading and unloading?
faq.a: A 14 ft truck reverses into tighter docks and smaller MSME yards. A 19 ft truck needs more reversing space but loads faster with fewer hand-stacks.

14ft-vs-32ft-mxl.title: 14 ft vs 32 ft container: Which Truck to Book?
14ft-vs-32ft-mxl.description: Compare 14 ft vs 32 ft container trucks on payload, volume and rate. On Kolkata–Rourkela (420 km), FTL is ₹35,700–₹50,400 and PTL ₹7,140–₹10,080/tonne.
14ft-vs-32ft-mxl.keywords: 14 ft, 32 ft container, truck comparison, which truck to book, PTL truck size

faq.q: How much can a 32 ft multi-axle container carry vs a 14 ft?
faq.a: The 2026 benchmark class rate for 32 ft multi-axle containers is 18–25 tonnes, against 2.5 tonnes for a 14 ft class truck — roughly eight to ten times the payload.

faq.q: Is a 32 ft multi-axle always cheaper per tonne?
faq.a: On full loads, yes — one 32 ft trip replaces several 14 ft trips, so the per-tonne cost is a fraction. For a quarter load, a shared 14 ft or a PTL consolidation on a 32 ft is usually better value.

faq.q: Where can a 32 ft multi-axle NOT go?
faq.a: It needs a long straight reversing area and cannot enter small city lanes, factory yards with tight turns, or low-clearance docks. It is a corridor vehicle, not a last-mile vehicle.

faq.q: What is the PTL option on a 32 ft multi-axle?
faq.a: LoadSaathi's PTL model lets several shippers share one 32 ft container on the same corridor, so each pays for the space they fill rather than the whole truck.

19ft-vs-32ft-mxl.title: 19 ft vs 32 ft container: Which Truck to Book?
19ft-vs-32ft-mxl.description: Compare 19 ft vs 32 ft container trucks on payload, volume and rate. On Bhubaneswar–Kolkata (440 km), FTL is ₹37,400–₹52,800 and PTL ₹7,480–₹10,560/tonne.
19ft-vs-32ft-mxl.keywords: 19 ft, 32 ft container, truck comparison, which truck to book, PTL truck size

faq.q: When does a 19 ft truck stop making sense?
faq.a: Once your shipment approaches the top of the 7–10 tonne class, a single 19 ft truck is at its limit and the per-tonne premium grows. A 32 ft container or a PTL share of one is then cheaper per tonne.

faq.q: How do the per-km rates compare?
faq.a: 19 ft/22 ft runs ₹36–₹48/km; 32 ft multi-axle runs ₹55–₹70/km. The 32 ft costs more per km but carries 18–25 tonnes against 7–10, so the per-tonne cost is well below the 19 ft's when reasonably full.
A 19 ft truck fits standard truck-loading docks. A 32 ft container needs a bay or ground-level ramp with a forklift; most MSME facilities can receive it at ground level.

open-vs-container.title: Open 19 ft vs 32 ft container: Which Truck to Book?
open-vs-container.description: Compare Open 19 ft vs 32 ft container trucks on payload and rate. On Jamshedpur–Kolkata (280 km), FTL is ₹23,800–₹33,600 and PTL ₹4,760–₹6,720/tonne.
open-vs-container.keywords: Open 19 ft, 32 ft container, truck comparison, which truck to book, PTL truck size

faq.q: Open body or container — which is cheaper?
faq.a: Open-body 19 ft/22 ft runs ₹36–₹48/km; a 32 ft multi-axle container runs ₹55–₹70/km. For weather-tolerant cargo an open body is usually cheaper; a container adds protection, and on a shared PTL the cost difference narrows.

faq.q: Can a container be loaded from above?
faq.a: No — only through the end door. If your cargo is crane-loaded or top-loaded, an open body is the right choice.
Containers reduce transit risk for sensitive cargo, which can lower claims. Open body needs good lashing and sheeting against weather and theft.

container-vs-trailer.title: 32 ft container vs Trailer: Which Truck to Book?
container-vs-trailer.description: Compare 32 ft container vs Trailer trucks on payload and rate. On Kolkata–Bhubaneswar (440 km), FTL is ₹37,400–₹52,800 and PTL ₹7,480–₹10,560/tonne.
container-vs-trailer.keywords: 32 ft container, Trailer, truck comparison, which truck to book, PTL truck size

faq.q: Container or trailer — which protects cargo better?
faq.a: A container is weatherproof and lockable, so it protects FMCG, paper and export cargo from rain and pilferage. A trailer is open, so it suits cargo that tolerates weather or is lashed and sheeted.

The benchmark classes are 18–25 tonnes for a 32 ft multi-axle container and 30–40 tonnes+ for a 40 ft multi-axle trailer. The trailer also takes over-width, over-height and over-length cargo a container door cannot.

faq.q: What loading equipment does each need?
faq.a: Containers load through the end door with a forklift, ramp or crane. Trailers load from above with a crane or from the rear with a forklift — no door-width constraint.

faq.q: Which is cheaper for a part load?
faq.a: For a part load, a shared PTL service on either body type spreads cost across shippers. A partially loaded container is often best for compact, weather-sensitive cargo.
